title: Price-Tier Triggered HC Phasing Playbook — Nov 2026
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is an operational budgeting playbook mapping demand tiers (traffic/usage) to a phased headcount plan and pricing sensitivity matrix. Intended for Finance + Eng leaders to translate near-term customer volume signals into hiring triggers and pricing actions.

Executive summary:
- We define three demand tiers (Contraction, Base, Expansion) and link each to a recommended HC cadence over the next 9 months, plus a set of price-move windows.
- The model favors pausing incremental hiring first (product/infra) before core SRE/ops cuts because of SLA risk.
- Pricing moves are conservative in Contraction, opportunistic in Expansion. We show the expected revenue delta under price adjustments and the headcount breakpoints where unit economics flip.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline ARR (run-rate as of Oct 2026): $128.4M.
- Monthly token throughput baseline: 1.9T tokens/month.
- Average revenue per 1M tokens: $52 (blended across hosted/dedicated).
- L2 cost per 1M tokens (infrastructure + amortized model licenses): $18.
- Hiring ramp: junior IC fully-burdened cost = $140k/year; mid-senior = $220k/year; manager = $320k/year.
- Hiring lead time (offer→ramp): 10 weeks average for ICs; 14 weeks for senior/manager.
- Elasticity estimate (observed from Q2–Q3 pilots): -0.45 for hosted price moves in the first 90 days, dampening to -0.30 over 1 year.

Demand tiers and triggers:
- Contraction: >5% MoM negative usage for 6 consecutive weeks OR top-50 customers show >10% aggregate usage decline month-over-month.
- Base: +/-5% MoM usage noise band. No hiring changes recommended unless pricing actions triggered.
- Expansion: >7% MoM positive usage for 6 consecutive weeks OR two or more customers >25% growth month-over-month.

Phased headcount plan (9 month horizon) — gaps and triggers:
- Purpose: Prioritize deferrable roles (hiring freeze for product growth roles) and preserve critical ops/SRE baseline.

ASCII table (monthly incremental hires by role under each demand tier):

| Month | Contraction (net hires) | Base (net hires) | Expansion (net hires) | Notes |
|-------|-------------------------:|-----------------:|----------------------:|-------|
| M1    | -2 (pause offers: 2 PMs) | 0                | +4 (2 infra, 1 product, 1 sales) | immediate freeze in growth hiring if Contraction |
| M2    | -1 (reopen offers only for critical SRE) | +1 (junior eng) | +6 (add 2 eng, 2 infra, 2 cs) | review pipeline after month end |
| M3    | 0                       | +2               | +8                   | consider limited contractor conversions in Expansion |
| M4    | -2 (voluntary separation buffer) | +2        | +8                   | hiring manager approvals tightened in Contraction |
| M5    | -1                      | +3               | +10                  | target >70% utilization for new infra hires in Expansion |
| M6    | 0                       | +0               | +6                   | freeze lifted if Base for 2 months |
| M7    | 0                       | +1               | +4                   | scale sales hires in Expansion after retention check |
| M8    | 0                       | +1               | +2                   | focus on onboarding capacity in Expansion |
| M9    | 0                       | 0                | +0                   | reassess at quarter close |

Note: negative numbers imply headcount reductions/hiring pause; actions should be coordinated with People Ops and Legal.

Pricing sensitivity matrix (summarized):
- We test price changes at [-10%, -5%, +5%, +15%, +30%] applied to hosted API blended price. The short-term (90d) elasticity is -0.45 applied; long-term (12mo) uses -0.30.

ASCII table (short-term revenue delta by demand tier):

| Price move | Contraction revenue delta | Base revenue delta | Expansion revenue delta | Note |
|------------|--------------------------:|-------------------:|-----------------------:|------|
| -10%       | -6.2%                    | +4.5%              | +13.1%                | price cut to defend volume — Contraction still loses rev |
| -5%        | -3.1%                    | +2.1%              | +6.5%                 | targeted promo for mid-market |
| +5%        | +1.8%                    | -2.3%              | -4.5%                 | MRR lift in Contraction customers with low elasticity |
| +15%       | +6.0%                    | -6.7%              | -13.4%                | risky in Base/Expansion; may drop adoption |
| +30%       | +10.9%                   | -15.2%             | -28.6%                | significant churn risk in Expansion |

Method note: deltas combine price change * elasticity and expected churn/compensatory volume shift across product tiers. Results are scenario outputs from the pricing simulation (see linked model).

Unit economics and break-even headcount thresholds:
- For every incremental senior infra hire ($220k fully-burdened), assuming incremental capacity reduces unit cost by 1.3% and revenue grows 1.8% in Expansion, payback ~9–11 months.
- Break-even customer volume for maintaining one SRE (~$220k cost) without worsening unit economics: ~45B tokens annual incremental throughput at current unit margins.

Actionable runway rules (operational triggers):
1) Hiring pause: if Contraction tier persists for >8 weeks, freeze non-critical hiring and reassign open reqs to hiring review board.
2) Pricing defense: in Contraction, authorize up to -5% short-term discounts for named customer retention (C-level approval required beyond -5%).
3) Expansion allocation: for sustained Expansion (>10% MoM for 2 months), accelerate infra and CS hires by 25% of planned pipeline (up to 12 heads total).
4) Pricing opportunism: in Expansion, test +5% price in new cohorts only (not retroactive) and monitor early churn signals for 30 days.
5) Headcount reductions: only after People Ops & Legal sign off, use a 3-tier assessment (risk to SLA, revenue impact by customer cohort, and internal critical skills).

Risk register (high level):
- SLA degradation if SRE cuts exceed 2 FTEs — downtime/latency exposure could trigger churn >6% among top customers.
- Pricing increases during Expansion may accelerate competitor substitution for price-sensitive customers.
- Hiring pause can slow product roadmaps leading to longer-term revenue opportunity loss.

Quick sensitivity example (one-pager):
- Scenario: Base → Contraction over 2 months; top 20 customers drop average 8% usage.
- Immediate steps: 1) freeze offers for PM/SE growth roles (M1 action); 2) run targeted retention discounts for top 10 at -3% (up to 90 days).
- Expected outcome: short-term ARR impact -1.9% vs baseline; mitigated churn to -1.1% with targeted discounts; net headcount delta -2 over quarter.

Implementation checklist (owners and timing):
- Finance: refresh rolling 9-month cash runway model with updated elasticity inputs (owner: Priya) — due Nov 12.
- People Ops: prepare redeployment options and voluntary separation allowance template (owner: Leila) — due Nov 18.
- Eng Managers: identify non-critical reqs to pause (owner: Marco) — due Nov 9.
- Sales/CS: build retention discount approval path and reporting (owner: Ethan) — due Nov 15.

Open questions for leadership forum:
- Tolerance for price increases in new customer cohorts during Expansion vs risk to net dollar retention?
- Do we have appetite for a temporary, targeted discount program in Contraction months funded from the reserve bucket? (see Finance reserve playbook)
- Are there key contractual obligations (enterprise discounts or committed capacity) that prevent rapid price moves? (Legal)

Appendix (extracted cells from the modeling sheet):
- Baseline unit margin (blended) = 65.4%
- Incremental gross margin improvement per infra hire = 1.1–1.5% (modeled range)
- Median time-to-productivity (junior) = 14 weeks; senior = 10 weeks (note: recruiting backlog can shift these).

Notes on governance and next steps:
- This playbook is intentionally pragmatic and short-term oriented; it should be mapped to the canonical 18-month headcount plan in Confluence.
- Next update: run the scenario with live usage telemetry after EOY close (target Jan 2027) and reconcile to dedicated/reserved revenue buckets.

Document version history:
- v0.1 (2026-11-05) initial draft by Priya
- v0.2 (2026-11-18) added elasticity short-term assumptions (Ethan)
- v0.3 (2026-12-02) incorporated People Ops feedback and revised hiring lag (Leila)

End of sheet.
